unitName.zh: 小于 1 与大于 100 的百分数

set.title: Percents below 1% and above 100% · Unit Test

questions.question: Each hundredths grid is a 10 × 10 square that stands for one whole (100%). Maya fully shades 2 grids, then shades 25 of the 100 small squares on a third grid. What percent has she shaded in all?
questions.explain: Each full grid is 100%, and each small square is 1%, so 100% + 100% + 25% = 225%. The trap is reading the shading as a decimal (2.25) and writing 2.25% — remember 2.25 wholes means 225 parts per hundred.

questions.question: Write 3.25% as a decimal.
questions.explain: Percent means 'per hundred', so divide by 100: 3.25 ÷ 100 = 0.0325 (move the decimal point 2 places left). The most common trap is moving it only one place and getting 0.325, or just dropping the % sign and leaving 3.25.

questions.question: What is 150% of 60?
questions.explain: Change 150% to 1.5, then multiply: 1.5 × 60 = 90. Watch out for multiplying by 150 instead of 1.5 (9 000), or adding 50 instead of taking 50% more (110).

questions.question: A credit union in Kamloops pays ½% interest per year on a youth savings account. Which value is equal to ½%?
questions.explain: ½% = 0.5% = 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005 = 5/1000 = 1/200. The classic mistake is to keep the ½ or 0.5 and forget to divide by 100, or to divide only once and land on 1/20, which is really 5%.

questions.question: A small town on Vancouver Island has 8 400 people. Over one year the population increases by 3.25%. What is the new population?
questions.explain: An increase of 3.25% means multiplying by 1.0325: 8 400 × 1.0325 = 8 673 (or 8 400 + 273). Two traps: stopping at the increase itself (273) and turning 3.25% into 0.325 instead of 0.0325, which gives the far-too-big 11 130.

questions.question: A school fundraiser in Surrey raised $1 400 000. The organizers donate ½% of the total to a local food bank. How much is donated?
questions.explain: Write ½% as 0.005, then multiply: 0.005 × 1 400 000 = $7 000. The big trap is treating ½% as ½ (or 50%) and getting $700 000 — a percent below 1% is a tiny slice, much less than one hundredth of the total.

questions.question: An esports club in Kelowna grew by 150% during the school year. It now has 200 members. How many members did the club have at the start of the year?
questions.explain: A 150% increase means the new amount is 250% of the original, so original × 2.5 = 200, giving 200 ÷ 2.5 = 80 members (check: 80 + 120 = 200). The most common error is dividing by 1.5 instead of 2.5, which forgets the original 100% that is still there.

questions.question: Owen buys a collectible hockey card for $80. In the first year its value rises 150%. In the second year the new value falls 40%. What is the card worth at the end of the two years?
questions.explain: Apply the changes one at a time to the amount you have at that moment: $80 × 2.5 = $200, then $200 × 0.6 = $120. The big misconception is combining the percents first (150% − 40% = 110%) and applying that to $80 — percent changes act on different starting amounts, so they cannot simply be added or subtracted.
